reconcile.note: Gill takes Deuteronomy's testing language of to know as revealing the heart to onlookers, since God already knew it and needed no test to acquire that knowledge.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza reads the false-prophet law at face value: God tests so that He may know whether the people truly love Him.

quotes.text: for the Lord your God proveth you, and that prophet shall be put to death." … "For the Lord your God tempts you, that He may know whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your mind.
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part II, trans. R. H. M. Elwes (1883), ch. VI, on Deuteronomy 13:3.

sides.snippet: to prove you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not.
sides.verseText: You shall remember all the way which Yahweh your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to prove you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not.

sides.snippet: who know the hearts of all men
sides.verseText: They prayed, and said, \"You, Lord, who know the hearts of all men, show which one of these two you have chosen
